title: Blind spot: it’s not just about capital, it’s about how you structure it
body:
When discussions turn to financing Africa’s green industrialization, they too often end with a familiar refrain: more capital.

Yet in practice, the binding constraint is rarely how much finance is available—it is how that finance is structured.

Many green energy and industrial projects fail not because they lack ambition or technical viability, but because they are built on the wrong financial architecture.

Too often, they rely on:

- Short-term, high-cost capital to finance long-lived industrial projects
- Unmanaged foreign exchange exposure
- Climate finance instruments poorly aligned with the realities of industrial development

Without an appropriate financial structure, even well-designed green power and industrial projects risk becoming stranded assets.

What Africa needs, therefore, is not simply more capital, but patient, locally aligned, and purposefully designed blended finance that:

- Matches the long time horizons of industrial transformation
- Mitigates foreign exchange, demand, and market risks
- Actively supports domestic manufacturing and the creation of industrial demand

In short, financing green industrialization is not just about availability—it is about design.

The real question, then, is not whether Africa can access capital, but whether it can structure finance in ways that transform energy systems and industrial production simultaneously.

Elvis K. Avenyo (Ph.D.) Emmanuel Buadi Mensah Woubet Kassa, PhD Solomon Owusu Victor Osei Kwadwo, Ph.D.
